paper.title: On Characterizations for Language Generation: Interplay of Hallucinations, Breadth, and Stability
paper.summary: Characterizes exact, approximate, exhaustive, unambiguous, and stable language generation; develops general uniqueness lower bounds, statistical consequences, and weaker notions of coverage. The registered definition surface preserves the literal exact-breadth, approximate-breadth, raw-stability, and infinite-coverage conventions. Lean proves incompatibility for several registered literal readings of stable fresh-support claims; mapping those readings back to the pinned source remains disputed pending named human correspondence review.

formalization_scope.summary: All numbered original main results in Sections 3–8 have source-facing Lean proofs or counterexamples. Of 31 registered cards, 24 have full positive coverage under the documented reading and 7 have counterexamples to the literal assertion or construction.
specializations: Countable-universe equivalences concern set-valued supports. Effective witnesses use normalized distributions on encoded words and specify oracle and ordinary computability hypotheses.
The corrected stable exact result changes from literal unseen support to whole-target support after restoring observations and is not counted as coverage of the printed theorem.
gaps: Five printed raw-stability claims have counterexamples. For Section 8.3 the source explicitly switches to sample-allowing coverage, and both the positive theorem and the literal impossibility are proved.

Literal Definition 3.1 exact breadth and Definition 8.3 infinite coverage are incompatible with raw-support stability on complete infinite presentations; Lean refutes the registered literal readings rather than formalizing them, while source correspondence awaits named human confirmation.
Theorem 4.5 stable exhaustive necessity fails on the full language and its co-singletons.
The two Figure 4 characterizations remain open in the paper. Additional literal counterexamples concern the rightmost column label and the generator printed in Example 8.12.

claims.title: Exact breadth, approximate breadth, raw stability, and infinite coverage impose distinct support obligations
claims.statement_summary: For a support-valued generator, Definitions 3.1, 3.2, and 8.3 require their respective support conditions eventually on every exact presentation, with a target- and presentation-dependent threshold: exact breadth is support equal to the unseen target K minus the current sample; approximate breadth is support contained in K with finite K minus support and does not remove the sample; and infinite coverage is an infinite support contained in K and disjoint from the sample. Definition 3.14 separately says that, on each single run, all sufficiently late raw supports are pairwise equal; it neither supplies correctness nor requires a common limit across presentations.

source_assessment.notes: Each definition has a literal semantic Lean endpoint. The qualification concerns their later conjunctions: exact breadth removes an ever-growing sample, and infinite coverage is likewise sample-disjoint, so neither literal obligation is compatible with eventual constancy of the raw support on a complete presentation of an infinite target. WholeTargetCorrectAt is a separately named Lean repair for the source's later sample-restored convention; it is not Definition 3.1 and contributes no coverage to this card.

formalization.notes: Nine canonical endpoints expose the stage predicates, fixed-generator eventual quantifiers, and the exact- and approximate-breadth existential class wrappers. All thresholds occur after the target and exact presentation and may therefore depend on that run. WholeTargetCorrectAt is deliberately excluded: it formalizes a coherent later repair, not the literal K minus sample equality in Definition 3.1.
